page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor. It delivers 2 dedicated virtual CPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Virtualized on KVM, the configuration includes hardware cryptographic AES acceleration but lacks x86-specific vector extensions. The instance has no bundled local storage and connects through a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses or integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements place the instance at moderate to entry-level processing capability within its resource envelope. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution reached an average score of 1824.28, while multi-core performance scored 3617.67, falling into the lower quartile. Memory throughput measured 26.08 GB/sec for large block reads and 16.11 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific metrics show 2.83 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 2.7 GB/sec static web throughput, and 58.25 tokens per second for small 135M parameter LLM text generation.

With its dedicated ARM cores and low resource footprint, ecs.c6r.large offers predictable execution without the unpredictability of burstable CPU models. However, the absence of local storage necessitates reliance on attached network storage volumes, and total throughput is capped by the 1 Gbps network baseline. This server is suitable for lightweight ARM-native application hosting, low-traffic web serving, basic Redis caching, and modest microservice deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor and 4.0 GB of RAM. Based on KVM virtualization, this configuration delivers a 1:2 core-to-memory balance alongside hardware AES cryptographic acceleration. It includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks place single-core CPU execution at an average level with 1824.28 points in stress-ng, while multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and compression metrics rank in lower brackets. Redis operations reached 2.83 million SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 2.7 GB/sec. Operating on dedicated ARM cores without hyperthreading or burstable penalties, ecs.c6r.large provides stable, predictable execution for lightweight web serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and basic in-memory caching workloads.
